statement: Finiteness of the rank-4 class for cons3 => sat. Let A be a positive 1-in-3 clause matrix (m x n) of GF(2)-rank 4. Write A = B C with C (4 x n) of full row rank, so every row of A equals b_i C for a unique nonzero b_i in GF(2)^4. Hence (a) A has at most 15 distinct nonzero clauses, and (b) the nonzero column types of C (variables with identical incidence columns) number at most 15, each with multiplicity at most 3 (a clause has 3 variables). Both cons3 (duplicating a column does not change solvability of Ax=1 over GF(3)) and sat (at most one copy of each type is switched on) depend only on the type-level structure, so the whole rank<=4 class reduces to a finite family of type configurations independent of n. Does cons3 => sat hold on every such configuration? Exhaustive n<=8 covers only configurations with at most 8 types, so it is a partial check. Next step: enumerate type-level configurations up to GL(4,2) symmetry.

The abstract states the same. Theorem 1.4 is the circuit-depth theorem (TC0, NC1, P/poly), not the streaming one. So contract row C's 'Thm 1.3' is correct and the owner note's 'Thm 1.4' is wrong for this statement. The ~N^{1+eps} vs poly(s) wording in the intro refers to total time and space, which is a different regime from per-bit update time. Earlier run cm-0c77b124288a43d1 is NOT evidence: its loop searched n < 10^7 while the claimed poly(s) < N^eps crossing needs log* n > d/eps (about n > 2^65536 for d=3, eps=0.5), so it could never return a hit.

label: aafa455048d3df13
statement: CAND-A quantifier check of (40a), spec v0.25 section 8.1 (page 8 read). (Q1) (40a) is written as 'for all M in M^unif_{s,A}, for all c,d, for all m0, exists m>=m0: S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d'. This is the correct negation shape for 'infinitely often' failure of every uniform machine, and it is ALSO the form Prop 13 needs. But the box FIXES s and A only in the sentence before it ('for some admissible s,A'); the existential over (s,A) is not in the box, so the statement is 'exists s,A: (40a)'. CORRECT as a premise only with an explicit 'exists s,A in PH admissible' prefix. (Q2) The class M^unif uses 'the same output and oracle conventions as in [4]'. MMW Thm 1.2 (per the ledger, Sigma3SAT^A oracle streaming with O~(s), O~(s^2)) means that if M may query the oracle, the premise is FALSE outright. So (40a) must range over ORACLE-FREE uniform machines (A only inside the synthesized circuits). WRONG as written; corrected reading: M^unif = uniform one-pass machines with no oracle access to A. (Q3) Negation of (40a) = exists M, c, d such that for all large m, S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d. This is 'eventually', not 'infinitely often'. Strength of (40a) is therefore 'for infinitely many m' (the weaker, i.e. easier-to-satisfy-the-negation side); check which one Prop 13 needs. (Q4) (8) => (40a): the exponent change c,d -> c',d' is harmless (the box is quantified over all c,d). a.e. vs i.o. is the point to check against the proof of (40). (Q5) S_M, tau_M worst case over all 2^m-bit inputs including the final report: not stated in the text; needs a definition. OPEN: whether P=NP yields an oracle-free uniform one-pass machine with S<=s^c and tau<=s^d at every large m. The natural route (store the truth table) costs 2^m space, not s^c; the MMW route needs the oracle. Prop 13's chain is therefore not verified as written.

statement: CORRECTION to my earlier gap list. MMW19 Thm 1.2 gives, for every oracle A and time-constructible s(n) >= n, a one-pass streaming algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s] with worst-case update time O~(s^2), space O~(s), and Sigma3SAT^A oracle (proof of Sec. 4: O(t) calls of length O~(t) between consecutive bits, t = Theta(s log s)). This is poly(s) update time, so Thm 1.2 does not block Thm 1.3. The n-dependent oracle B_n of Thm 4.1 is a separate linear-time construction and is NOT needed for Thm 1.3; my earlier 'gap (a)' was a misreading and is withdrawn. The amortised-vs-worst-case point is also moot, since Thm 1.2 already states worst-case update time. OPEN OBLIGATION (unchanged, not progress): Thm 1.3 needs the HYPOTHESIS, a fixed A in PH with no poly(s)-space, poly(s)-update-time streaming algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s]. Thm 1.2 supplies an upper bound only; the hypothesis is a lower bound and remains unproved. Scope: source reading of MMW19 Thm 1.2 and Sec. 4-5 proofs; no new theorem.

statement: CORRECTION to S-30387c5b68 / cm-7d4a9766b4c043d2: the 'min width' there is the EXACT minimal width of the fixed order 1..n, max over cuts of the number of distinct subfunctions (Myhill-Nerode), not a GF(2) cut rank. It is a fixed-order quantity only, so it is not the minimal width over all orders. The reachable width counts distinct (state, modulator) pairs and is an upper bound on the minimal width for that order. Evidence: 0 violations over w=2, n in {8,10,12}, k in {2..n}, 200 trials each. Open: no family in which the measure drops below the product bound has been found. Structural lemma: a plastic ROBP (w states, k modulators, budget T) is an ordinary ROBP of width w*k*(T+1), so the state count alone cannot separate the plastic model from fixed-width ROBPs. The enrichment must come from a measure other than state count: description cost of the update rule (k*w*2 entries, growing with n when k=n), uniformity across n, or re-coding cost.

statement: REDUCTION of the one-tape seed barrier (Q-5226caddf1, step 1). Set N = 2^n, machine input length N, time t = N^{1.01}, q states. Spec: Viola decomposition gives a sum of n-input ROBPs of width W = exp(O(sqrt(t)·log(tq))) (the spec's exponent is garbled; the sqrt(t) reading is the one used by Q-5226caddf1 and must be source-checked against Viola's paper). A Nisan/Forbes-Kelley-type generator for length-N ROBPs of width W has seed O~(log W) (Forbes-Kelley: O~(sqrt t)·log q here). So the seed is governed by log W, and the magnification target seed <= N^{mu'} for small mu' with t = N^{1.01} is equivalent to log W(t) <= t^{eps} for eps <= mu'/1.01. So the route needs the single lemma: a decomposition of time-t one-tape q-state DTMs into ROBPs over N input bits with log W <= t^{eps}·polylog for every eps > 0 (or for some fixed small eps). Viola's exponent 1/2 is the obstacle. Two open sub-points: (a) is log W >= Omega(t/N) (crossings per input cell) a lower bound for this decomposition, which would be harmless for t/N <= t^{eps}, i.e. only when N >= t^{1-eps}, which is not our regime N = t^{1/1.01}; (b) whether a non-ROBP generator (not via Nisan-type seeds) can beat log W. CONJECTURE, not proved. Mark as open; do not claim a route to N^{1.99} for small mu.

statement: CORRECTION to HYPOTHESIS S-3f9e1f1795 (nullity-growth route): the stated 'hypothesis' that nullity grows linearly for m/n < 1 - eps is a tautology. Since rank_3(A) <= m, nullity_3(A) = n - rank_3(A) >= n - m > eps*n, so linear growth holds by definition. The 3^nullity bound is only an enumeration cost of the affine space, not a difficulty measure, because deciding whether that space contains a 0/1 point is the hard extraction step (D-018) and is not addressed by counting. A real test would need a claim about the 0/1 search itself, for example the number of 0/1 points or the search cost in the affine space, measured on a fresh dense dataset.

The 3^nullity bound is only an enumeration cost of the affine space, not a difficulty measure, because deciding whether that space contains a 0/1 point is the hard extraction step (D-018) and is not addressed by counting. A real test would need a claim about the 0/1 search itself, for example the number of 0/1 points or the search cost in the affine space, measured on a fresh dense dataset.

The n=4 case is the complete 3-graph K4^(3): all four 3-subsets of a 4-set, which is unsatisfiable because for an omitted vertex v the intersection size is |S| - [v in S], which cannot equal 1 for all v. Is every unsatisfiable positive 1-in-3 formula with at most 4 distinct clauses a superset of some K4^(3) on its support? Test: for each unsat m=4 formula at n=5,6,7, check whether its clauses contain four triples on a common 4-set. A formula with no such 4-set is a counterexample and would show that K4^(3) is not the only minimal obstruction at m=4.

Thm 1.3 hypothesis as written is 'poly(s) space and poly(s) update time'. The intro also gives a total-time example (N^{1+eps} total time, N^eps space), so MMW19 itself uses both quantifiers; the formal Thm 1.3 uses update time. CLAIM: Let F be a finite CNF over n Boolean variables, with clauses interpreted as disjunctions of literals. For each clause c, let A_c be the assignments that falsify c. For every subset S of clauses, the intersection of the A_c for c in S is empty if the falsifying requirements conflict; otherwise it has size 2^(n-|V(S)|), where V(S) is the set of variables occurring in clauses in S. Consequently #SAT(F) = sum over S of (-1)^|S| times this intersection size. The empty subset contributes 2^n; tautological clauses have empty falsification events; repeated literals are allowed.

statement: PRIORITY (owner 2026-11-21, P1 / M1.1, final form): EXTEND CHEN-TAL-WANG TO ARBITRARY POLYNOMIAL SIZE. Starting point: ECCC TR26-039 (March 2026) - f in E^NP needs n^{2.5-o(1)}-size THR o THR, via a faster CAPP algorithm for the XOR of two THR o THR circuits + Williams' algorithmic method (spec_read('PNP-001-LIT-7-2026-11-21.md'); strategy spec_read('PNP-001-GRAND-STRATEGY-2026-11-21.md')). GOAL: keep a running-time advantage for GENERAL polynomial-size instances, giving E^NP (or NEXP) not in THR o THR. TRANSFER CONDITION (mandatory, source-check first): Williams' transfer needs an algorithm for a class PROVEN sufficient - it must absorb the extra combination of circuits used in the transfer (here an XOR of two); Chen-Oliveira-Santhanam (CCC 2019) give sufficient conditions, e.g. a non-trivial SAT algorithm for polynomial-size THR o MAJ circuits - state the exact theorem before designing anything. Known decomposition of the 2.5 (to verify): ~sqrt(m) F2 probabilistic degree of the SYM gate (exponent 2) + random restrictions leaving ~1/sqrt(n) of the THR gates non-constant (Kane-Williams, +0.5). TASK: (1) exact transfer theorem; (2) an algorithm for the sufficient class with exact running time, or the exact step where the CTW technique stops for larger sizes; (3) lab tests of sub-steps on small circuits only as evidence. Consequence: a new circuit lower bound - NOT P != NP. Barriers are checked against this transfer only (relativizing proofs are acceptable here). Mark PROVED / SOURCE / CONJECTURE.

Precise claim structure: if rewriting an unsatisfiable CNF to the zero diagram is a proof system P (each step checkable in polynomial time), then the MINIMAL size of P-refutations bounds from below the certificate size, hence the work of EVERY procedure that outputs P-certificates. Consequence check: a superpolynomial lower bound for this ONE system proves neither NP != coNP nor P != NP (that needs every proof system - Cook-Reckhow); state exactly what the result would imply. Literature mappings to source-check before use: decision-DNNF compilation vs regular resolution (Beame-Li-Roy-Suciu 2013), holographic algorithms and planar #CSP (Cai-Lu-Xia 2010). Mark every step PROVED / SOURCE / CONJECTURE.
